requirement:
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every
item without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, except items inside a module named `tests`. A warning MUST NOT fail
validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Each obligation has an `{impl}` reference and a test that asserts its outcome.

**Obligations and code**
- **`habeas status` warns about every item without recent coverage, naming file, line, kind and name.**
  - `src/commands.rs#fn[coverage_warnings]` renders the "Coverage warnings" section. It is called from `status_markdown_with_github`.
  - It takes the uncovered items from `inspect_repository` and filters them through `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[warnings]`.
  - Each item's text comes from `uncovered_error` in `src/rust_coverage.rs`, in the form `file:line: kind name has no recent coverage…`.
- **`habeas author` warns after it finishes.**
  - `src/main.rs#fn[print_coverage_warnings]` calls `src/commands.rs#fn[coverage_warning_lines]`.
  - `main` calls it after the batch summary, after the "evidence is current" skip, and after the single-subject run.
  - The warnings go to stderr, and a failure to compute them is reported without failing the command.
- **Items inside a module named `tests` are excluded.**
  - `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[in_tests_module]` sets `in_tests` on each uncovered item.
  - `warnings` drops those items with `!item.in_tests`.
- **A warning does not fail validation.**
  - Uncovered items are kept in `RepositoryInspection.uncovered`, separate from the report's errors.
  - The warning functions only print them.
- **Repository validation does not read Git history.** Only `warnings` calls `RecentCoverage::load`, and only the status and author warning paths call `warnings`. Validation never calls it.
- **Cited `coverage.history` behaviour.**
  - `warnings` filters by `covers_selector`.
  - Both warning paths report incomplete history: `coverage_warnings` adds a "Coverage history is incomplete" paragraph, and `coverage_warning_lines` adds a note line.

**Tests**
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item]` covers the following:
  - An unread `helper` is warned about at once.
  - The `fixture` helper inside `mod tests` is not warned about.
  - `parse` is not warned about until the fourth version.
  - Validation reports no error for the warned item.
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete]` covers the following:
  - Status shows the warning line for `render`.
  - Status omits a covered item.
  - Status says history is incomplete in a shallow clone.
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[habeas_author_prints_coverage_warnings_on_stderr]` checks that `author --all` prints the warning on stderr and not on stdout.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject]` checks the author warning on the skip-as-current paths.
- `tests/coverage.rs#fn[validation_does_not_read_git_history]` removes the Git object database. Validation errors stay the same, and `coverage_warning_lines` then reports that history is incomplete.

All of these tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.

text: :::{req} coverage.report
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every
item without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, except items inside a module named `tests`. A warning MUST NOT fail
validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.
:::{req} coverage.history
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
the commands of {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report` MUST say that
coverage history is incomplete.
:::{example} coverage.reauthored
Function `parse` has no reference, and the evidence of `requirements.cli.check`
read it. The requirement is re-authored and committed twice, and neither new
record reads `parse`. With the default window of 3, the record's third most
recent version still names `parse`, so `habeas status` does not warn. After a
third such commit, no version in the window names it, and `habeas status` warns
about `parse`. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.new_function
A new function `helper` has no reference, and no evidence record has ever read
it. `habeas status` warns about it at once; nothing in any window names it.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.test_module
A helper function inside `mod tests` has no reference and is read by no record.
`habeas status` does not warn about it. A `#[test]` function in the same module
without a `{test}` reference is still a validation error.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.tests`
